title: CARICOM, bridges and borders: Belize and the Guianas look outward
goal: Describe how Belize and the Guianas connect with their neighbours, and where borders are still in question, with aun cuando.
grammar: concessive clauses with aun cuando and the subjunctive

sections.title: CARICOM, bridges and borders: Belize and the Guianas look outward
body: In this lesson you read about how Belize, Guyana and Suriname belong to CARICOM, the Caribbean community, and how bridges and agreements are starting to link them with Brazil and with the Amazon countries. You also read where borders are still in question.

The grammar is one you know: *aun cuando* "even when, even if". The screens and instructions are in English; the readings are in Spanish. (Belize, Guyana and Suriname are not Spanish-speaking countries: their official languages are English and Dutch.)

items: I can grant a point with *aun cuando* and the indicative for a fact, or the subjunctive for a possibility.
I can say where CARICOM has its headquarters and which bridges were opened in 2009 and 2017.
I can use the new words for headquarters, bridges and borders.
